It would be good to add the object path and interface in the trace. If it will be added in some other trace then ignore this comment.
Done
not needed
Move this variable to private area

`If the position isn't on D-Bus, or if the value is maxint, consider
  the position to be 0xFF.` --> The type of `bmcPosition` should be  `uint8_t` not `std::optional<uint32_t>`

Good point, thanks. Done.
Also turns out it simplifies things to not store it as an optional due to some refactoring due to other comments.
I want to be able to set/get the value for testcases. I could have get/set functions but I think now the thing to do is just leave it public.
Consider to move `init()` method to constructor of `BMCPosMgr`
Done, though had to add a unit test check into the D-Bus call so that it doesn't spit out errors every time the class in instantiated.
Consider to remove setBMCPosition/getBMCPosition, we can use `bmcPosition` directly inside this class.

Ended up refactoring things a bit based on the comments, so this function behaves a bit differently now.  Would still like to call it from logManager so still needs to be public.  Can continue the  discussion of this in that file if necessary.

This action is redundant, the init() method is called in the constructor of `manager`, if you are afraid of missing `Decorator.Position` interface in the constructor, I think you can create matcher to monitor `Decorator.Position` interface

I will look into it.  I am worried that there could be some case where a signal would be missed.  It would also have to watch both InterfacesAdded and PropertiesChanged, which is extra work for something that is only error case for us.

I tried to use both IA and PC signals to get the position if it isn't available right away, but since Position will be coming from PIM for us, and PIM doesn't emit signals when it is restoring its cache, then the code will never end up getting a position except for the first boot when it's added.  So I don't think I can avoid explicitly making the call.
Changing to just read it from a file which will be quick.
Suggestion: init could called inside `BMCPosMgr` constructor.
Done
We should check the `use-bmc-pos-in-id` is enabled or not before compile this file, check others
I followed the bmcweb method of still compiling everything and using the 'if constexpr (USE_BMC_POS_IN_ID)' checks instead of #ifdefs everywhere.  Unless you feel strongly I'd like to keep it.
License statement is missing?
Done
hmm, don't need this anymore.

Do we have any deadlocks here where phosphor-inventory-manager can't create logs because we'll end up calling back into phosphor-inventory-manager, which isn't listening because it is waiting for the log to be recorded?

(or similar with entity-manager, mapper, etc.)

I don't see PIM ever creating logs.
EM though will probably start using lg2 to commit those 'inventory added' logs.

I'm not sure how likely it is that EM would host this Position interface on this object path, but if it did and somehow got far enough along before phosphor-logging started, then I could see this issue:
1. EM makes lg2::commit call to create 'inventory added' log
2. D-Bus activation starts phosphor-logging
3. on startup, phosphor-logging tries to read the BMC position from EM
4. Deadlock?  Or does the async call that EM uses prevent that?

Any ideas? How bad would it be if we just stored the position in a file as well?  That would simplify this code quite a lot.
Going to resolve this because EM would be my only worry and it would be using async or asio.
Since EM would after all be using the sync version of commit, I think a deadlock would be possible. I'll explore getting the position into a file in /run/openbmc/
Done, I moved to reading it from a file.
Why put this logic here?  Can't it be handled in the bmcPosMgr?
Yes, should be possible, will fix.

With the other commits also adding function into this leg: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-logging/+/84858/4/log_manager.cpp#228  it makes it harder to push things into the BmcPosMgr since this class will be doing things.

So I will resolve this but am open to any better solutions.
Why make this a public API?  Can't `processEntryId` do this internally?  It seems like a better encapsulation to have it all done in the BmcPosMgr.

Other commits add more log_manager functionality into this path so it can't be all done inside processEntryId (unless I pass logManager in).
1. removing old logs with no position if there is now a position (a new log manager function)
2. setting entryId so that it picks the next one after the last log with the current BMC position. (looks at the entries map)

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-logging/+/84858/6/log_manager.cpp#226 shows the full code
Abandoned the commit with 1., but the usecase for 2. still holds.
Ack.  I don't necessarily agree, but it's fairly minor and this is your repo to maintain. ;)
Not sure yet why CI didn't catch this, but it's needed since this test uses log_manager.
Due to meson option defaulting to false?
